prompt.brief: Design an ML demand-forecasting platform that predicts daily, weekly, and monthly demand across thousands of SKUs and locations while handling seasonality, promotions, stockouts, and external signals.
successSignals: Version sales, inventory, pricing, promotion, calendar, weather, and external features with an explicit data-cutoff time.
Train global and SKU-level candidates, reconcile store-region-national forecasts, and prevent future information leaking into features.
Serve a versioned forecast snapshot quickly while training, backtesting, and late data correction remain asynchronous.
Explain stockout censoring, cold-start SKUs, uncertainty intervals, overrides, drift, approval, and reproducibility.

functional: Ingest demand and feature data, define forecast horizons and hierarchies, train candidates, and publish approved forecasts.
Query forecasts, confidence intervals, model version, feature cutoff, backtest metrics, and manual overrides.
Support backfills, corrections, scenario forecasts, access controls, lineage, retraining schedules, and export.
nonFunctional: Target MAPE below 15% on agreed segments while reporting bias, coverage, and error by horizon and hierarchy.
Train thousands of series in parallel without allowing one large category or backfill to starve daily publication.
Make feature snapshots, training runs, model promotion, and forecast publication idempotent and reproducible.
Serve the last approved forecast with an explicit stale marker when feature feeds or training workers fail.
scaleAssumptions: Forecast 100,000 SKU-location series across daily, weekly, and monthly horizons.
Partition training by product and geography, isolate high-volume series, and keep feature windows bounded.
Retain feature snapshots, labels, forecasts, model artifacts, overrides, and evaluation evidence for replay.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the ML demand-forecasting platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional ML demand-forecasting platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return ML demand-forecasting platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition ML demand-forecasting platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound ML demand-forecasting platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for ML demand-forecasting platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable ML demand-forecasting platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable ML demand-forecasting platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure ML demand-forecasting platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines multi-horizon forecasting, hierarchy reconciliation, stockouts, scale, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and SKU/location/horizon keys support forecasts, promotions, stockouts, privacy, overrides, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain ML demand-forecasting platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
